topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Hallmarks and Progression
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the lecture objectives, historical hallmarks framework, and the general paradigm of cancer as a progressive loss of growth control.

topics.label: Sustaining Proliferative Signaling and Evading Growth Suppression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations across cell-surface receptors and downstream cascades drive autonomous proliferation and override inhibitory growth cues.

topics.label: Blockade of Terminal Differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how tumors in both hematopoietic lineages and epithelial tissues sustain expansion by obstructing normal cell maturation pathways.

topics.label: Evasion of Apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the molecular mechanisms and regulatory balance between pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins that allow cancer cells to resist programmed cell death.

topics.label: Replicative Immortality and Senescence Bypass
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how telomere attrition induces stress-mediated senescence and how tumor cells activate telomerase machinery to achieve unlimited replication.

topics.label: Deregulating Cellular Metabolism
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the functional shift toward aerobic glycolysis and the production of oncometabolites that reinforce malignant progression.

topics.label: Inducing Tumor Angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the physiological requirement for neovascularization to prevent hypoxia and the regulatory switch governing blood vessel recruitment.

topics.label: Invasion and Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the sequential biological hurdles, dissemination patterns, and genomic features enabling cancer cells to colonize distant tissues.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Closing
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer provides concluding perspectives on the interconnected nature of cancer hallmarks and closes the session.
